title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report
hook: Taobao's recommender now reasons about intent, not just click history. V3's trick: do that reasoning in compact latent tokens instead of long chain-of-thought, cutting output-token cost 200x at production scale.
key_points: RecGPT-V1 and V2 moved Taobao's recommender from behavior-pattern matching toward reasoning about user intent; V3 targets three scaling pains: stateless reprocessing, a lossy tag-to-item bottleneck, and slow explicit reasoning.
A Memory Hub keeps structured, continually-updated user memory instead of reprocessing full history each request, cutting user-modeling compute by 55.8%.
A Hybrid-modal Foundation Model reasons jointly over natural-language tags and Semantic IDs (SIDs), giving a higher-bandwidth channel from language into concrete items.
Latent Intent Reasoning compresses verbose chain-of-thought into compact, learnable latent tokens that stay decodable into readable explanations — cutting output-token cost 200x.
Deployed in Taobao's 'Guess What You Like' feed, online A/B tests report IPV +1.28%, CTR +1.00%, GMV +3.97%, and 52.4% lower end-to-end serving resource use.
content_html:
RecGPT started as Taobao's bet on recommendation-by-reasoning: instead of just matching co-occurrence patterns in past clicks, model what the user actually wants. V1 proved the idea; V2 scaled it with coordinated multi-agent reasoning. Running that at real production scale, per this report from Bowen Zheng and a large Taobao team, surfaced three separate pain points — recomputing a user's whole history on every request, a natural-language "tag" layer that loses information on the way to actual items, and chain-of-thought reasoning too slow and expensive to run at scale.

RecGPT-V3's answer to each: a Memory Hub that maintains condensed, continually-updated user memory instead of reprocessing everything from scratch (55.8% less user-modeling compute); a hybrid-modal foundation model that reasons over both text tags and Semantic IDs so item grounding isn't squeezed through a lossy tag bottleneck; and Latent Intent Reasoning, which compresses the model's reasoning into compact latent tokens instead of long written-out chains of thought, while keeping those tokens decodable back into human-readable explanations. The authors report a 200x cut in output-token cost from that last piece. Deployed in Taobao's "Guess What You Like" feed, they report consistent online A/B gains — including GMV up 3.97% — alongside a 52.4% drop in end-to-end serving resource use.
extra_html: What stands out is less any single technique than the combination being validated at Taobao's production scale rather than on a benchmark — a rare public look at how a major e-commerce recommender is re-architecting around LLM-style reasoning without paying LLM-style inference costs. Full report linked via the source.

related.title: Reading Between the Dots: Hidden Computation in Filler Tokens
related.hook: Frontier models can solve multi-step problems while outputting nothing but dots — no visible reasoning at all. This paper shows that 'hidden' computation is still legible, just not in the output.

related.title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning
related.hook: When you can't afford to let every query think as long as it wants, who gets the compute? Treat reasoning tokens like a scarce resource and economics gives a clean answer.

flashcards.prompt: What three scaling problems does RecGPT-V3 target that V1/V2 didn't solve?
flashcards.back_html: Stateless behavior modeling (reprocessing full user history every request), a lossy tag-to-item information bottleneck, and inefficient explicit reasoning with high latency and compute cost.

flashcards.prompt: How does Latent Intent Reasoning cut RecGPT-V3's output-token cost by 200x?

choices.text: It internalizes verbose reasoning into compact learnable latent tokens that remain decodable into explanations, instead of writing out long chain-of-thought
It skips reasoning entirely and returns cached recommendations
It shrinks the model's parameter count to speed up decoding
It batches many users' requests into a single forward pass

flashcards.explanation_html: Rather than generating lengthy explicit chain-of-thought text, RecGPT-V3 reasons in a small set of learnable latent tokens that still decode back into readable rationale when needed, avoiding the token cost of verbose reasoning.

flashcards.prompt: What does RecGPT-V3's Memory Hub replace, and what compute saving does it report?
flashcards.back_html: It replaces reprocessing a user's full history on every request with structured, continually-updated user memory, cutting user-modeling computation by 55.8%.
